findings: baseline: all 11 scenarios met their expectation, and all 35/35 checkable properties held.
no_jev: all 11 scenarios met their expectation, and all 35/35 checkable properties held.
with_jev: all 11 scenarios met their expectation, and all 35/35 checkable properties held.
caveats: Natural-language planning versus a hand-built plan: no measurable difference. The gap of +0.0017s is smaller than the run-to-run spread of 0.3359s.
Adding JEV (mocked): no measurable difference. The gap of -0.0032s is smaller than the run-to-run spread of 0.3384s.
The full pipeline versus a hand-built plan: no measurable difference. The gap of -0.0015s is smaller than the run-to-run spread of 0.3342s.
Timings are from small synthetic workbooks on one machine; they are not a production performance claim.
JEV was mocked, so no network latency, provider reliability, or cost is represented. A live call, if authorised, is recorded separately under `live_jev` and is never blended with these numbers.
No quality score is reported, because there is no ground truth against which to score one. Scenarios with a checkable property assert it instead.
The planner is fully deterministic, so planner variance is zero and the planner is not a source of the timings above.

The baseline is the same planner with its plan truncated to one operation. It isolates the surrounding machinery, not planning quality, which this benchmark cannot measure without a reference answer to plan against.

live_jev.note: A single live integration call was made with explicit authorisation. It is an integration validation artifact, not a benchmark sample. It is excluded from every benchmark aggregate, comparison, and performance figure in this document.
live_jev.result_summary: One live call was made and returned four decisions. Two were selected with high confidence (automation=approval_required p=0.97; risk=medium p=0.97). Two were returned as needs_review at 0.5 probability (interpretation=requires_user_input; verification=value_check). No error was reported. Because any needs_review raises scrutiny, this result would escalate rather than authorise. This is a single sample: it demonstrates the integration works end to end against a live provider, and establishes nothing about accuracy, reliability, or latency distribution.
